title: ohnapse settings
description: Configuration for the ohnapse CLI, stored at .ohnapse/settings.json.

$schema.description: URI of this JSON schema, for editor validation.

model.description: Which account and model the agent uses.

provider.description: Profile name: the key under 'providers' holding the account this run uses. The name is your own label and selects a host and a credential, not a wire format. A profile named after a dialect ('anthropic', 'openai', 'azure', 'google') also settles the dialect by name; any other name has it discovered from the host, or pinned with providers.<name>.api.

id.description: Model identifier passed to the endpoint (e.g. 'claude-sonnet-5', 'gpt-4o', 'gemini-1.5-pro'), spelled the way the host spells it — run 'oh models' to list them. For Azure this is informational; the deployment selects the model.

maxTokens.description: Maximum tokens to generate per response. Provider default when omitted.

probe.description: When to measure an endpoint's real capabilities before trusting them. auto: measure a profile/dialect/host/model combination the first time it is seen. off: never measure implicitly; only 'oh doctor' probes. always: measure every run.

thinking.description: Extended reasoning. Off unless budgetTokens is set, and skipped entirely when the provider does not report a thinking capability.

budgetTokens.description: Token budget for reasoning. Omit or set 0 to disable thinking.

stripInlineTags.description: Treat <think>...</think> in ordinary text as reasoning, for OpenAI-compatible servers that lack a dedicated field. Default false: a false positive would swallow real output.

providers.description: Connection details per profile, keyed by the profile name used in model.provider. A profile is an account — a host and a credential — so one block serves every model that account exposes. Secrets are read from environment variables first (OHNAPSE_API_KEY_<PROFILE>); the fields here are an optional fallback.

permission.description: Autonomy tier plus per-tool allow/deny/ask rules. Rules are evaluated deny > allow > ask, then the tier default.

tier.description: Session autonomy. read-only: only reads. auto-safe: reads + in-workspace edits auto, exec/network confirmed. full-auto: everything auto (sandbox still enforced).

allow.description: Rules that auto-approve matching tool calls.

deny.description: Rules that block matching tool calls outright (highest precedence).

ask.description: Rules that force a confirmation prompt for matching tool calls.

sandbox.description: Kernel sandbox tuning (Landlock on Linux, Seatbelt on macOS).

network.description: Permit outbound network access from sandboxed tool executions. Default false.

additionalDirectories.description: Extra directories the sandbox may write to, beyond the workspace and a temp dir.

maxToolCalls.description: Hard per-run tool-call budget (backstop against runaway loops). Default 50.

maxParallelTasks.description: Widest delegation fan-out run at once. Overflow runs in the next wave. Default 4.

agents.description: Sub-agent roles available to the task tool, added to (or replacing by name) the built-in explore and coder.

circuit.description: When the agent stops itself because it is looping. Each value is how many times a shape must repeat before the turn ends. Omit a field or set 0 for the default; values below the minimum are treated as the default.

identicalFailure.description: Stop after this many consecutive identical (or near-identical) tool errors on the same target. Default 3; values below 2 use the default.

editThrash.description: Stop after this many edits or writes to one file that oscillate (A then B then A) or do not change its contents. Default 3; values below 2 use the default.

noProgress.description: Stop after this many consecutive tool calls that change no file and produce no new result. A varied search is progress. Default 8; values below 3 use the default.

theme.description: Color theme for the interactive UI. 'mono' disables color, as does setting NO_COLOR in the environment.

env.description: PLANNED (accepted but not yet enforced): environment variables injected into tool executions.

hooks.description: PLANNED (accepted but not yet enforced): commands to run on agent lifecycle events.

mcpServers.description: PLANNED (accepted but not yet enforced): MCP servers to connect for extra tools.

providerSettings.description: Connection details for one profile. Which fields are meaningful depends on the dialect the profile turns out to speak.

api.description: Pin the wire dialect this profile speaks. An escape hatch: leave it out and the dialect is taken from the profile name, or discovered by asking the host what it serves. 'bedrock' is planned but not yet implemented.

baseURL.description: API base URL. Overrides the adapter default: an endpoint implementing one of the supported wire formats, a gateway fronting several model families, or a self-hosted deployment.

apiKey.description: API key fallback (environment variable is preferred). Stored in the git-ignored .ohnapse directory.

accessKeyId.description: AWS access key id (Bedrock only; planned).

secretAccessKey.description: AWS secret access key (Bedrock only; planned).

capabilities.description: Override the adapter's feature defaults for this endpoint. Each field is optional; omitted fields keep the built-in default. Run 'oh doctor' to see what the endpoint actually supports.

parallelTools.description: More than one tool call can arrive in a single turn.

agentDefinition.description: One sub-agent role the root agent can delegate to.

name.description: Name the model passes as the task tool's agent argument.

description.description: What this role is for. The root agent reads it when choosing.

prompt.description: System prompt for the sub-agent's own run.

tools.description: Tools this role may use. The task tool is never included, so a sub-agent cannot delegate further.

readOnly.description: Run without mutating tools, which also lets any number of these run in parallel regardless of scope.

permissionRule.description: A tool name, or a tool name with a glob over the call's target. Globs support ? (one char), * (within a path segment), and ** (across segments). Examples: 'read', 'edit(src/**)', 'edit(.git/**)', 'exec(git *)'.
